name: Value stack (what you get)
look_note: The stack reads best as the lander look's 2-up grid of panels; the branch's separate proof row is the renderer's trust line.

sources.name: Alex Hormozi, $100M Offers: value equation and Grand Slam offer stack

sections.hero: Dek: the outcome the ad promises, with less effort or time -- no number unless verified.
sections.items: Each item is one concrete part of the offer the reader gets, not a vague benefit.
sections.faq: Answer what is and is not included, and what costs extra.
sections.closing: Recap the stack in three bullets; the fixed warranty and financing sentences follow.

items.heading_hint: The core product that delivers the main outcome
A built-in part other options sell separately
How fast it is ready to use (setup, power, preheat)
What it asks of the reader day to day (space, assembly, use)
An extra that comes in the box -- only when verified
Delivery, warranty and support terms that come with it

voice: Direct and concrete, second person, short sentences; name the part, not the feeling.
compliance: Every number, price, spec or outcome needs a verified claim_id; a hint is never a fact.
No health or outcome promise for the product; a health statement cites the study and its population.
No invented dollar value on any part of the stack.
writer_brief: Adapt the stack to the ad's angle: each item is one concrete part of what the reader gets, backed by a verified claim. Keep it short.
